# NIDS – ML-Based Network Intrusion Detection System

A lightweight Network Intrusion Detection System. It turns network traffic into flow features and
classifies each flow into **benign or one of 12 attack classes** with a soft-voting ensemble of
**LightGBM, XGBoost and CatBoost**. Every alert comes with a plain-language explanation built from
per-feature SHAP contributions. Alerts appear on a real-time Flask dashboard with authentication,
role-based access, and a tamper-resistant incident log.

**Project site:** `index.html` (GitHub Pages). All results on the site are generated by
`nids/train.py`; see `nids/reports/metrics.json`.

## Repository layout

```
index.html, assets/        project website (results.js / report.js are generated by training)
nids/features.py           28 live-computable flow features + bidirectional flow builder
nids/train.py              data pipeline, training, evaluation, model integrity manifest
nids/detector.py           SHA-256-verified model loading, ensemble prediction, SHAP explanations
nids/capture.py            traffic sources: live Scapy capture, held-out replay + attack simulation
nids/app.py                Flask dashboard, Flask-Login, RBAC, CSRF, SQLite incidents + audit log
nids/models/               trained models, manifest.json (hashes), replay.csv.gz
nids/reports/metrics.json  full evaluation output
```

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10–3.12.

```bash
python -m venv .venv && .venv\Scripts\activate        # Linux: source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

# 1. (optional: trained models are already included) retrain on CIC-IDS2017
#    Download MachineLearningCSV.zip to data/raw/, then:
python -m nids.train

# 2. create the database and first admin account
python -m nids.app init

# 3. start the real-time dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:5000
python -m nids.app run                    # replay of held-out flows + attack simulation
python -m nids.app run --source live      # real packet capture (Npcap on Windows / root on Linux)
```

## Dataset

[CIC-IDS2017](https://www.unb.ca/cic/datasets/ids-2017.html), `MachineLearningCSV.zip`
(2.83 M labelled flows). Duplicates are removed before the stratified 80/20 split to prevent leakage.
Infiltration and Heartbleed are excluded because they have too few samples (36 and 11).

## Security design

- **Authentication:** Flask-Login; scrypt password hashes; 5 failed logins per IP → 5-minute lockout.
- **Authorisation:** viewer < analyst < admin, enforced per route, deny by default.
- **Web hardening:** CSRF tokens on every POST, strict CSP (no inline scripts), X-Frame-Options DENY,
  HttpOnly / SameSite cookies (`NIDS_HTTPS=1` adds Secure), binds to 127.0.0.1 by default.
- **Data integrity:** parameterised SQL only; triggers make the audit log append-only and incidents undeletable.
- **Model integrity:** joblib files are SHA-256 verified against `manifest.json` before loading.
- **Privacy:** only flow metadata is processed; payloads are never stored.

## Limitations

The live flow builder approximates CICFlowMeter, so accuracy on traffic from a different network will
be lower than the test-set figures until the model is retrained on local labelled data. Web
brute-force and XSS flows look alike at the flow level, and the dataset has few examples of them.
